newsitem.title: USA: PSA 'encouraged' by likely delay of stadiums bill.
newsitem.headline: PSA 'encouraged' by likely delay of stadiums bill.

text.p: A PSA official said Monday the group is "encouraged" by word late Friday that Sen. Daniel Patrick Moynihan probably will change the June 14, 1996, effective date of his stadium financing bill to whatever date a new bill is introduced early next year.
"It's important and encouraging," Micah Green, executive vice president of Public Securities Association, said in a telephone interview.

"If the senator is now making it clear to the marketplace that the June 14 date is going to change, that is an extremely helpful sign to the marketplace that projects currently underway can move forward," Green said.
But Green said PSA hopes Moynihan, D-N.Y., takes his plan to ease the bill's effective date one step further by changing it to the date any bill actually clears Congress.
"If the bill is introduced in January with (a January) effective date it will have the same chilling effect that June 14 had," Green said. "It would freeze the marketplace dead in its tracks.

Green predicted no rush to market if the effective date is changed to the date any bill is finally enacted. "The marketplace will have (had) time to assess whether or not this legislation would actually move," Green said.
A congressional source told Reuters Friday, "When we reintroduce the bill in January, there is a good chance we will change the effective date."
"We're not sure what the date is going to be, but it won't be June 14," the source said. "If it gets changed, anything that's going on now will be exempted from it."
The source said Moynihan is considering revising the effective date to when it is reintroduced, possibly January 1997.
